Nitrogen Balance
Nitrogen balance studies are used primarily in research studies 
to estimate the balance between exogenous nitrogen intake 
(orally, enterally, or parenterally) and removal of nitrogen-
containing compounds (urinary, fecal, wound), and other 
nitrogen sources. These studies are not a measure of protein 
anabolism and catabolism because true protein turnover stud-
ies require consumption of labeled (stable isotope) protein to 
track protein use. Even if useful, nitrogen balance studies are 
difficult because valid 24-hour urine collections are tedious un-
less the patient has a catheter. In addition, changes in renal 
function are common in patients with inflammatory metabo-
lism, making standard nitrogen balance calculations inaccurate 
without calculation of nitrogen retention (Gottschlich et al,
